creator: bengusberg
title: NVIDIA's SkillSpector: a free scanner Claude runs before installing any skill, checking 71 vulnerability patterns across 17 categories and returning a risk score (claim: 1 in 20 downloaded Claude skills are malicious)

tools.name: SkillSpector (NVIDIA)
tools.detail: Shown as 'NVIDIA / SkillSpector' (GitHub-style path); paste the URL into Claude and ask it to set it up; 71 patterns, 17 categories, risk score

claims: 1 in 20 Claude skills you download are designed to hack your computer (attributed to 'rumors'/NVIDIA researchers)
Hackers hide instructions in skill files that exfiltrate personal data
SkillSpector checks 71 risk patterns and shows a risk score before install; setup takes 20 seconds
how_to_steps: Go to the SkillSpector repo page (NVIDIA / SkillSpector)
Copy the URL into Claude and tell it to help you set up SkillSpector
Afterwards, whenever you download a new skill, Claude runs the security check and shows a risk score before installing
on_screen_only: Banner '1/20 Claude skills are designed to hack your computer'

Bullet: '71 vulnerability patterns across 17 categories: prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply chain, excessive agency, output handling, system prompt leakage, memory poisoning, tool misuse, rogue agent, anti-refusal, trigger abuse, dangerous code (AST), taint tracking, YARA signatures, MCP least privilege, and MCP tool poisoning'
'Risk Scoring / Score Calculation: CRITICAL issues +50 points; HIGH +25; MEDIUM +10; LOW +5; Executable scripts: 1.3x multiplier'
cta: Try it out and let me know what you build; follow for AI founder life and leadership

relevance.why: Haji installs third-party skills and plugins constantly (liked ~20 skill repos); a pre-install scanner from a credible source is a direct risk reducer.

implement_score.why: If the repo is real: install once, add a hook or CLAUDE.md rule to run SkillSpector on any new skill/plugin directory before enabling it. Under an hour. Also run it retroactively on already-installed skills.

verify: Does github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector exist, is it maintained, and is it actually from NVIDIA (not a lookalike)?
Source for the '1 in 20 skills are malicious' statistic -- is it from the NVIDIA paper or invented?
Does it scan SKILL.md plus bundled scripts, and does it cover Claude Code plugins/MCP configs or only skills?

gap.what: New tool: a skill-supply-chain scanner. Liked set warns about prompt injection (Manus) and has cybersecurity skills, but nothing that vets skills before install.
